item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This really is There Is No Canon, isn't it?

Just to see if I'm getting all of this:

+ show block
– hide block

THE WORM is us, but not just in the sense of writers like Swann's Proposal, but in the wiki itself. Every SCP is another fencepost, and is another tiny fork creating another universe, all slightly different from one another - again, since there is no canon. Those that are low quality, poorly written or executed, have low universal integrity, end up being deleted, these days with formal votes once the "integrity rating" is below a certain level.

The nods to wiki history are there too - Iteration /X/, Iteration Editthis, and Iteration Wikidot, with the Mass Edit there as well - although I'm surprised there's not more meat to those tabbed sections, or any nod to a certain Fish vendor who was a cause of much drama around here.

Still, very good. I'm somehow a stick in the mud who thinks that meta stuff is too self-masturbatory, but still loves every bit of it he can find, and this was put together excellently.

I'm not sure what the significance of the first section (the page disappearing and reappearing) or the last one (Alternatives and below) are, though?

item.title: Re: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
This entry is magnificent, and I'm confused why you would put down such a good entry, especially one written in collaboration with others. The only thing wrong with it is the extra cruft attached to it, like the testing logs. This entry can stand on it's own without twenty links to existing and new articles, so let it. Less is more.

But when I say that's the only thing wrong with that, I really mean it. This piece itself is amazing. Wonderful idea of a ruthless Foundation, making copies of itself to delay (or will it?!) some sort of reality-eating entity which cannot currently be seen, much less understood or fought. The writing was also excellent. It also explains how everything on this site can be as it is. I would have liked more direct explanation of what the worm was, though I'm pretty sure I've figured it out correctly and that in any case it is mostly a matter of personal preference.

Easily earns a place among the other excellent 001's!

I really enjoyed this; the prose itself is extremely polished, the idea is both horrible and has a cruel internal logic, and the execution has a number of clever turns. It also neatly explains a lot of incongruities with the setting without relying on some sort of hackneyed third-act "THE FOUNDATION ISN'T REAL!" twist. It felt a little bloated to me at certain points, but that's likely just coming down to personal taste.

There's a lot of thematic and mechanical elements here that are similar to a tale series I've been messing with off and on for about a month, now. Presuming it's alright, I might want to use some of this stuff (or even ask you a couple of questions about it at some point in the future!).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This has been quite the trip, and as Moose said, it was an odd piece of fiction to write. I view this as almost like an alternative fiction "What if?" version of the SCP canon that was a lot of fun to speculate about, even if none of us ultimately agreed with this version of history.

It took a lot of work to translate our original version into what you see today, and I have to thank Moose for taking the brunt of the effort with regards to reworking the entire piece, as well as Dex and Drew for reviewing the work we put together. Ultimately, I think we've come up with something that's much stronger overall, and hopefully tells the story of Palisade that we intended from the very start.

item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
This was a strange SCP to write, rewrite, and repost. It is an SCP I disagree with. I do not believe it is, or should be, canon. I don't agree with its premise. I disagree strongly with its moral universe. Even though I'm responsible for its thematic backbone. It is not part of anything I've written outside the Doomsday Contest.

This may not make sense to anyone, but my parts of this were heavily inspired by SCP-3999, the collective works of djkaktus starting with "O Death" onward, the works and perspectives of many long-gone site members, and a hell of a lot of deleted SCPs.

This piece would not exist without Dexanote, Drewbear, and weizhong. weizhong wrote the entire myths section, and edited the entire piece extensively. Drewbear wrote the original history (and brought in all the Bowe stuff), and made many fixes. Dexanote shaped the original idea, before (and while) I went off the deep end with it. All three read and edited the piece before posting.

Thank you to Modern_Erasmus, Petrograd, Toa_Vine, Ihp, and TL333s for leaving valuable feedback on the original article. This version was massively, massively rewritten, and I hope the piece works better.

Special thanks to DrEverettMann for edits and contributing a text suggestion (a poem excerpt).

This is part of the Project Palisade storyline, which is, at least for now, complete. So hopefully this doesn't go down in flames!
